ab_managed_not_solved.description: Kill the Sinkhole Lurkers along the Long Collapse and the Limestone Crawlers between there and camp, and bring Odd the lurkers' spurs.
ab_managed_not_solved.accept_text:
Peska wants the readings. Hask wants his method. Vizzi wants a floor under every rope.

I want the camp to still be here in a month, and that is a different list and it is mostly killing.

I am not going to dress it up. Go and make the ground round this peg quiet for a while.

That means the sinkhole lurkers and the limestone crawlers. Kill both, and bring me the lurkers' spurs so I can show Peska the count.

ab_the_long_collapse.description: Walk the north rim of the Long Collapse for Odd, kill the Sinkhole Lurkers denning there and bring back their spurs.
ab_the_long_collapse.accept_text:
The Long Collapse opened eleven months ago, over about four hours, and it took twenty-two tiles of ground and a stretch of the old road with it.

It is the only one any of us watched happen. I want the rim walked and I want it walked by somebody who is not me, because I have walked it nine times and I have stopped seeing it.

The Long Collapse is south-west of camp, on past the Wide Sink. Sinkhole lurkers den under the rim. Kill the ones you meet and bring me their spurs - Peska says the spur tells her how deep they came up from.
ab_the_long_collapse.turn_in_text:
You can walk the whole length of it and never be more than a step from the edge. Three years ago that was road, and I'd have driven a cart down it.

Peska put that in the book in my words. She doesn't usually write that way, but she said the measurements alone didn't cover it.

barrows_hunt_king.description:
I've been watching that hill since the hounds went quiet.

At the end of the Barrows lies Hunt-King Valorin.

Still hunting. In his sleep, which is a sentence I've written in three reports now and had queried every time.

Here's what it means in practice, and it's why I won't leave it alone.

The Wild Hunt never ended. It went underground - the whole apparatus of it, the king, the road, the hounds, the horns - and it has been running down there uninterrupted for as long as that hill has stood.

And a hunt ranges. That's what a hunt is. It does not stay within a boundary because the boundary is new and the hunt is not.

I will not have a dead king's hunt ranging over Horde land because nobody wanted to go into the hill.

Let's make sure it stays underground.
barrows_hunt_king.turn_in_text:
He rode out of the world a long time ago.

Now he's finally ridden all the way home.

I can stop watching that hill now.

barrows_rimebone_cull.description:
Veyra. I scout the Barrows for the post, and I want them quiet, and I'd like to tell you precisely what I mean by quiet because it isn't a figure of speech.

That hill sings.

Not loudly. You have to be on the north wall at the right hour, and once you've heard it you hear it every night after, which is its own problem and not one I'll trouble you with.

It's the Hunt's old song. And it keeps being sung because the Hunt-King's road is still being kept.

The rimebone hounds keep it. The wights keep it. They walk a route that has not changed in however many centuries and the walking is what holds the song together.

Break the route and the song has nothing carrying it.

Dead things in a cold hole. It is not complicated.

Go in with friends, come out with the job done.

barrows_wintermaw.description:
There's a hound chained in the Houndkeepers' Crypt the size of a warhorse.

Chained. That's the part worth sitting with - somebody put it there on purpose, and somebody wanted it to stay, and whoever that was has been dust for a very long time.

The chains are old.

The grudge is older, and I don't use that word loosely. I've tracked a lot of things and I can tell the difference between a beast that's angry and a beast that's been waiting.

It will not come to you.

That's the whole tactical content of what I've got. Everything else in that hill ranges - the hounds run the road, the wights walk it. This one stays where it was put and makes you come into the room.

So you will go to it.

Take a healer. And take a good reason, because you'll want one about halfway down the stair.

sb_blind_hunter.description:
There's a hunter in the western galleries and I'd have called him a story six months ago.

He's been blind for years. Everyone in that hill knows it. And he does not miss.

I've lost two friends to him, scouts like me, good ones, both of them quiet, and quiet is exactly the wrong qualification against a man who's listening.

The second one was carrying nothing. No pack, no mail, soft boots, and he was taken clean through the dark at a range Oggra's best archer couldn't make with his eyes open.

So he isn't guessing. Something about that gallery carries sound to him and he has spent years learning the shape of it.

The handlers guide him. Take them - that's not a kindness to him, it's that a blind hunter who's being walked to you is a different problem from one who has to find you.

West gallery, past Aggem's pen.

He listens for you. Don't stand still.

And don't breathe loudly either, if it comes to that. I'm aware of how that sounds.
sb_blind_hunter.accept_text: Razorfen Kraul, south of Oggra's post. He keeps the west gallery, past Aggem's pen, and his handlers keep him.

sb_razorflank.description:
Top of the Kraul. A platform of bones, a hut of thorn and tusk, and Charlga Razorflank sitting in it.

She's heard the pens fall. She's heard the speakers die. Nothing you've done in that hill has been a secret from her and I'd rather you went in knowing that than thinking you had surprise.

The hill's heart is hers. That's not a flourish - the thorn on that ridge grows because she wants it to, and Oggra has four winters of measurements that say so.

Take it, and the thorns wither by spring.

Oggra's wanted to say that sentence to somebody capable of doing it since her first winter out there. She asked me to say it for her, and it's come out smaller than either of us expected.

Totemics around her. She mends them as fast as you cut them, so cutting them is a losing proposition and always has been.

Go for her first if you can.

The thorns won't forgive you for it. They'll stop, though.
sb_razorflank.turn_in_text:
Charlga's dead.

The Kraul will take a generation to recover, if it recovers at all, and that ridge will breathe for the first time since anybody in Taurajo was born.

Take this, with all the thanks Oggra has in her, and mine.

sb_seed_and_thorn.description:
Ashhoof. I scout for the camp, and these days mostly for Oggra.

The thorns on that ridge aren't wild.

I need you to take that seriously, because everyone Oggra reports to treats it as a figure of speech and it is a flat statement of fact.

The geomancers inside the Kraul seed them. One barbed pod at a time, pushed into the ground by hand, and I've watched it done through a glass from the second bend, on a scouting run for Oggra.

Every pod is a little more hill the quilboar own.

That's how a thornwatch loses a ridge - not in a battle. A pod a day for ten years, and then one morning you notice your post is a hundred paces inside somebody else's country.

I want pods for Oggra's notes, because a drawing is an opinion and a pod on a table is evidence.

And I want the geomancers who make them put in the ground.

They carry them while they work, and they're almost always down on their knees doing it.

Handle the pods by the stem. They open if you squeeze them, and they do not close again.
sb_seed_and_thorn.accept_text: Razorfen Kraul. Its mouth is south of Oggra's thornwatch post, where the thorn closes over the road. The geomancers work the ground just inside, on their knees.
sb_seed_and_thorn.turn_in_text:
The thorn's spreading faster than I'd feared.

And now Oggra can prove it to somebody who outranks her, which is the whole point.

sb_the_beast_pit.description:
Tull. I keep the camp's kodo, and I've been counting the ones that don't come back.

From the pens a narrow neck runs north-west, and it's sealed.

Not barred. Warded - stones set into the rock, held by Ward-Keepers who do nothing else, in a hill where everybody does three jobs.

That's the Beast Pit.

There's a thing in it called Agathelos, and they've been feeding it on stolen kodo for years. Our kodo, off that ridge, which is where a great many of Taurajo's missing animals went and nobody ever found a track.

The ward-stones keep it in.

So understand what I'm asking: break four and the ward falls, and then it is not in anymore.

I've thought hard about leaving it sealed. The seal is holding. But it's holding because quilboar maintain it, and the day they decide to open that neck themselves is a day they choose and not one we do.

Ward-Keepers hold the neck. Break the stones, then go in.

Agathelos is a beast, not a boar. Don't mistake one for the other. It isn't kind about that.
sb_the_beast_pit.accept_text: Down in Razorfen Kraul, south of Oggra's post. The warded neck is north-west of the pens. Break the stones first, then go in after Agathelos.

sb_the_pens_below.description:
At the centre of the Kraul are the Boar Pens.

A corral ring with stalls on every side, and in the middle of it Overlord Ramtusk, who has been fattening boars for a war for a decade.

Ten years. I want that number to land, because I've had it a while and it still does.

That's not a raiding herd. You don't need ten years for raids - you need a season and a bad winter. Ten years is somebody who has a date in mind and has had it since before Oggra took her post.

I keep war drums for a war that hasn't come. I want the pens broken before anybody opens them and it does.

Sows in the stalls, the Overlord in the ring.

The ring has three gaps. Hold the south one and they'll come to you through it - that's the only way this fight is manageable, because the open version is a hundred boars and no corners.

And keep the sows off your back. They'll come round while you're looking at him.
sb_the_pens_below.turn_in_text:
The Overlord's down and the pens are empty.

Oggra will sleep tonight. Four winters, and she'll sleep tonight.

sb_the_vine_bridge.description:
West of the first fork there's a rope-and-vine bridge over a drop, and on the platform at the far end lives Roogug.

He's been ordering that hill's warriors about since before Oggra was a ranger.

And here's the argument Oggra keeps having with her officers: he's off the main road.

Which makes him safe to leave alone. That's true, strictly. Nothing he does threatens the ridge directly and no patrol of hers has to pass him.

She'd rather he were not left alone, and so would I.

Because a quilboar who has been giving orders for thirty years and never once been tested is a quilboar everybody in there still listens to, and that's worth more to the Kraul than the ground he's standing on.

The bridge is narrow. Don't fight on it - that's how you lose a party one at a time.

Wait for them on the platform. Roogug will come to you.

He's all muscle and no plan. Use that.
sb_the_vine_bridge.accept_text: Inside Razorfen Kraul, south of Oggra's post. Take the vine bridge west of the first fork. Roogug holds the platform beyond it.

sb_two_speakers.description:
Rohan. I keep the camp's war drums, and while Oggra's out on the ridge I send people into the Kraul for her.

North of the fork the Kraul splits around the Thorn Court, and a chieftain sits at either end of it.

Aggem Thorncurse, west. He calls the boar-spirits.

Death Speaker Jargba, east. He speaks for the dead and - this is the part that matters - he takes what they tell him extremely seriously.

Oggra's spent four winters working out which of them actually runs this hill and the answer is neither, and that's why both have to go.

They keep the heartbeat. Between the two of them the whole warren knows what it's doing on any given day, and stopping either makes it stumble.

Whichever order you like. I've no preference and I'd be inventing one.

Aggem's guards are beast-trainers with boars. Jargba's are Death's Head, with hexes.

Don't fight both courts at once. The Thorn Court is open ground and it'll pull them together if you stand in the middle of it.

And don't let either one finish a sentence.
sb_two_speakers.turn_in_text:
Both of them!

I'd call the hill's spirit broken, but Oggra's been out there long enough to know better, and she'd tell me so.

Take this, and my respect.

splintertree_lord_malgan.accept_text:
A tyrant who loses a ritual has two choices open to him. Try again, or die trying.

I have buried enough grunts to know which one Malgan will pick, and I have no intention of letting him get far enough into it to find out whether I'm right.

He holds the Throne by fear now rather than by strength. That is not the same thing and the satyrs under him know it even if he doesn't - you can hear it in how they move when he's in the open.

So I'll make the choice for him. He's at the Throne. Go and take it away from him.

Satyr's Throne is north of Splintertree. He has not left it, and he will not.

splintertree_satyr_ritual.accept_text:
The satyrs at Satyr's Throne have been singing for three nights.

I have fought a great many things in this forest and I have learned their songs the way you learn any language - by listening to it being used for ordinary purposes until the unusual ones stand out.

That is not a song of welcome. It is not a song of mourning either, which was my second guess and which I would have preferred.

It's preparation. Something is being made ready at the Throne and the tricksters are leading the chant, which means the tricksters are the part that has to be carried.

Remove them, and the song has nothing to carry it, and whatever is being prepared stays unprepared a while longer.

spn_sd_lair.turn_in_text:
Air coming out of it. Warm air.

[He is quiet for a while.]

Then it isn't a cave, it's a way through to something, and this wood has been getting its weather from somewhere other than the sky.

That's beyond a webhunter. That goes to Vesk, and Vesk will send it on, and somebody with a better title than either of us can decide what to do about it.

And if you're going back into the Lair itself, see Bone-Carver Yseult. She's taken the rest of my list off me.

spn_wl_brood.description:
Yseult. I carve what the tombs give up, and lately what the Widow's Lair gives up.

Corvane the webhunter has been inside the mouth of the Lair. Not far in, but far enough to count, and counting is his job.

Hatchlings in the thousands.

He's said that figure out loud to three different officers and watched all three decide he was exaggerating. He wasn't. He counted a section and multiplied, which is how anybody counts anything that doesn't hold still.

And silk-bound weavers tending them, which is the part that should worry people more than the number.

Something in there is being looked after.

Thin the first rooms before anyone tries the deeper ones. That's the whole of this job and I'd not pretend it's more.

Hatchlings first. The weavers sit above them and spit, and you will not see the first one.

spn_wl_silka.description:
The hive buds off a single queen and her name is Silka.

West lair, off the Web Heart.

Here's what that means, and it's the reason I'm sending you at her rather than at the numbers.

Everything Longleg ever was came out of her eggs. Every spider in those woods that anybody has ever lost a dog or a child to - that's one line, from one source, and the source is still laying.

Corvane assumed for years that the woods simply had spiders. Woods do.

Then he counted, and his count only works if there's one.

End the line.

Follow the egg sacs west. They get thicker the closer you are, which I'd call helpful if it were anything else.

She's what they're all running from. I don't have a better way to put it and Corvane's watched them do it.

spn_wl_skitter.description:
There's a second queen-brood in the east lair, under a weaver called Skitter.

And she is not Silka with a different name. I want that clear before you go in with the same plan.

Silka lays. That's all she does - she's a source, and the hive flows away from her.

Skitter keeps.

She hangs her victims from the ceiling for later. Alive, some of them, for considerably longer than you'd think possible, and Corvane has been close enough to the mouth of that lair to establish that, and he wishes he hadn't.

He's watched it from the mouth for a season.

He'd like to stop watching it, and I'd like him to. That's the honest whole of my reason and it isn't strategic.

East of the Web Heart.

And look up before you step in. Not after. Before.

spn_wl_velaxis.description:
Above the Web Heart there's a spire, and Velaxis nests in it.

Older than Silka. Larger than Skitter. And not fond of company, which in anything else I'd call a personality and in her I'd call a warning.

She is the head of this hive.

Not the source - Silka was that. Not the keeper - that was Skitter. The head, meaning that both of those answered upward, and Corvane didn't believe spiders did that until he spent a season at the mouth of that place watching them.

Cut it off and the hive is a lot of legs with nothing arranging them.

Up the north neck from the Web Heart.

The Spire is lit by her eyes. That is how you'll know you've arrived, and it's the last useful thing I can tell you.

I'm not going to pretend this is anything but a death sentence for whoever tries it. Corvane has watched two go up that neck.
spn_wl_velaxis.turn_in_text:
Eight eyes, all closed.

I'll rest easy tonight, and so will these woods, and I'll tell Corvane he can finally put that word in a report.

You've earned every copper and a good deal more I haven't got.

sps_at_mages.description:
The reading hall is staffed by the dead, and I use the word staffed deliberately.

Kirin Tor and Forsaken mages who kept studying after they stopped breathing.

That's not a haunting. A haunting repeats. These are working - moving between lecterns, taking things down, putting things back, and the thing that finally convinced me was that the stacks are in order.

Somebody is shelving.

And there are imps bound to the lecterns, which tells you the binding was done by a living hand at some point, because an imp does not stay on a lectern out of professional interest.

I want the hall cleared so I can walk it.

The mages cast first - all of them, immediately, and they do not posture about it.

The imps hold the doors. Expect to fight your way back out as well as in.
sps_at_mages.turn_in_text:
I can walk it now.

Perhaps even a very brave librarian, and I know two.

sps_at_orrery.description:
One last thing and then the magister locks the door.

The Orrery is the Observatory's twin. East of it - a round room full of little worlds, all still turning.

Still turning. Nobody has wound anything in that building for decades and those worlds are keeping time.

That's what the waygate has been feeding, as far as I can establish. Not the lamps, not the wards. The models.

And here's the thing I've worked out and cannot explain: they go out when somebody stands in the room.

A living person, present, for about a minute. Then the lamps settle and the little worlds slow, and when you leave they do not start again.

I don't know what that means. I know I want it done.

Observatory first. Then the Orrery to the east.

Stand a minute in each. That's all. Just be there.
sps_at_orrery.turn_in_text:
Dark. Both of them.

The waygate sleeps.

Orsolo will lock it and give me the key, and I'll keep it somewhere stupid and not tell you where, because then three of us would know.

sps_at_vestibule.description:
Tamsin Hale. I scribe for Magister Orsolo, and with Quillfire silent he can finally say this out loud without somebody shouting it down. So can I.

That waygate was keeping something.

Everybody has treated it as a door nobody uses. A door nobody uses is a door that has been left - this one has been MAINTAINED, and the difference is visible from the outside if you know what a maintained ward looks like.

So something on the other side was worth the upkeep, and somebody was paying it until very recently.

The tower's lowest rooms are a vestibule and a reading hall above it.

Stand in both and tell me whether the lamps are still lit.

That's the entire ask and I know it sounds trivial. It isn't. Those lamps don't burn oil. If they're lit, something is still putting power into that building, and if they're violet, it is listening.
sps_at_vestibule.turn_in_text:
Still lit. Violet.

So it's listening.

Thank you. Truly. The magister's been arguing for permission to ask that question for two years, and I've been writing the letters.

sps_sfk_fenrus.description:
Fenrus was Arugal's first experiment and his least successful.

I've had that from two sources and neither of them was being kind about it. Least successful means it didn't do what he wanted - not that it failed, because it is very much alive down there.

He devours things in the crypt.

And nothing that goes in comes out. That's not dramatic, it's a tally - Marl's kept the gate nineteen years and he knows what's gone down that cloister, and what hasn't come back up it, and the two numbers are the same number.

Marl would like to be the exception, and so would I.

That's our whole stake in this. He's stood at that gate nineteen years watching things go into a hole and we'd like, once, for something to come back out of it on its own feet.

At the end of the cloister.

And mind the sarcophagi on the way down.

They breathe. I've been told that by three people and I've stopped asking them to explain it.

sps_sfk_guards.description:
Ashe. Field surgeon. I take things apart for a living, and Shadowfang has a few I'd like taken apart.

The keep's old guard never left their posts.

I'd call that loyalty if there were anybody left for them to be loyal to.

The guardsmen wail where they stood. Not where they fell - where they were POSTED, which I know because the positions make sense. Stand in the Great Hall and look at where they are and you can read the old watch order off them.

And the officers keep giving orders. To no one. Out loud, in the proper form, with pauses where the acknowledgement should go.

That's the part I can't get past, and it's why this is the job I'd most like done.

They were never relieved. Somebody should have come to take that watch and nobody ever did, and they are all still standing there waiting for it.

So relieve them. One way or another.

Officers first, then the men. That's the order it should have happened in and it's the only courtesy left to pay them.

sps_sfk_keys.description:
A practical one, and it'll make everything after it cheaper.

The haunted servitors still carry the keep's keys on their belts.

Every one of them. A full ring each - and they're not guarding the doors, they're simply still carrying what they carried, because that's what a servitor does and nobody ever took them back.

Right now the cloisters and the armoury are a gamble.

That's the actual situation, and I've stitched up what it costs. You come to a door in that keep, you don't know if it's locked, and you find out by standing in front of it long enough for something to arrive.

I'd like the doors to stop being a gamble.

The Great Hall and the cloisters. Servitors carry a ring each.

Take the ring, not the key. I want whole rings - a ring tells you which doors went together, and that's a floor plan, and nobody's ever had one of those.
sps_sfk_keys.turn_in_text:
The right doors, and none of them haunted.

Almost enough to make a person hopeful.

Almost.

sps_sfk_razorclaw.description:
Pell. Marl keeps the Shadowfang gate and I take his nights.

The Butcher's Yard is east of the bailey, and Razorclaw keeps it.

A worgen with a cleaver where a hand ought to be. Not holding one - instead of one, and I've had that confirmed by two people who got close enough to wish they hadn't.

Marl's heard the chopping from this gate for years, and I've heard it every night watch since I got here.

That's the whole of my case and I know how thin it sounds in a report.

It's regular. That's what nobody understands when I say it. It isn't a frenzy and it isn't a fight - it's the sound of a man working, at a steady pace, for hours, and then stopping, and then starting again the next day.

Something is being prepared in that yard on a schedule, and the schedule has not changed in all the time Marl's stood at that gate.

East of the bailey. Follow the sound.

You'll hear it from the gatehouse. Everyone does. Everyone decides it's something else.

pls_a_dispatch_for_sorrow_hill.accept_text:
The High Executor's written to the Order of the Pale Flame, and she's asked me to find somebody to carry it, because she won't walk across the street herself. Those banners over there are theirs. They kept a fort on Sorrow Hill until the hill got too dead even for them, and now they're inside our wall.

They wear what used to be Scarlet armour, and some of them used to burn our kind. They also kill the mindless dead and leave my patrols alone, and my patrols need every friend they can get.

Take it to their Flamekeeper, Rory Callahan. He stands at the keep's door on the south side of the Bulwark. Don't let him keep you talking.

pls_what_the_plague_is_made_of.accept_text:
Dorian's packed your samples into a case, and he's asked me to send it on, because he won't leave his bench while the Haunt's sample is still moving. He studied under Apothecary Merrow Vane. She's at Sun Rock Retreat in Stonetalon now, watching the dead get up on the Mulgore side of the mountain with nobody calling them.

He thinks it's the same sickness as the cauldrons. I've stitched up enough of what comes out of those fields to think he's right, and I'd like us both to be wrong.

Take the zeppelin from Tirisfal to Orgrimmar and a wind rider to Sun Rock. Merrow will be the only Forsaken there. Keep the case upright, and don't let the tauren open it, however politely they ask.

pls_the_school_under_the_island.accept_text:
You've seen the island in Darrowmere, the one with the dead trees and the lit windows. That's Caer Darrow. I knew the Barovs when they owned it. They sold it to the Cult of the Damned for a promise, and now it's a school. The Scourge teach necromancy there the way the Kirin Tor teach fire.

The headmaster is Darkmaster Gandling. Every necromancer who's put a skeleton back on its feet in Andorhal learned it in his halls. I held that town against his students for a year, and he kept making more.

He keeps his study at the bottom of the school, below everything else. You won't get there alone, so don't try. Head north-east out of the Bulwark and down to the lake, take your whole company, and come back and tell me the school's closed.
pls_the_school_under_the_island.turn_in_text:
The school's closed, then. They'll open it again one day, they always do, but not this year.

Rory came through in the Integration with a welding ticket and a bad knee, and he's the one who taught me you can shut a school. I'll tell him tonight.

pl_ts_crusaders_insignia.description: Bring Quartermaster Hollis Burke a handful of Crusader's Insignia from the Scarlets of the Plaguelands.
pl_ts_crusaders_insignia.accept_text:
Every Scarlet in the Plaguelands carries a Crusader's Insignia, a red flame on a white field. Odile used to count them, and now the Order's asked me to, since I'm the one who pays for them.

The Scarlets camp all round Andorhal, south-east of the wall, and every one of them carries a badge. Every badge is one fewer fanatic burning somebody's farm. Bring me a handful whenever you have them. I'll write each one down for Odile's book, and then the smith melts them into buckles.
pl_ts_crusaders_insignia.turn_in_text:
That's a handful of fanatics who won't be lighting anything tonight.

Here's the Order's thanks, and some of its coin. Bring me more when you've got them.

ple_word_to_lights_hope.accept_text:
Captain Varden wrote this report and then gave it to me to carry, the same as he did at Crown Guard. Back then I ran it up the road and wondered whether I'd get there. Now it's a walk across the square, and he still won't hand it over himself, because Dawnbringer asks questions.

It says the Crusade at Tyr's Hand is moving. I'd carry it myself, but the captain wants me on the road watch.

Take it to Commander Eligor Dawnbringer. He stands on the chapel steps at the top of the town. Wait while he reads it, because he'll have something for you.

ple_a_word_with_the_order.accept_text:
The Commander's written to the Order of the Pale Flame, and I wrote it down for him. They're Scarlets who walked out of the Crusade, and they kill only the mindless dead. Some of the Dawn don't trust them. He'd like to, and so would I.

Their Flamekeeper, Rory Callahan, knows the Crusade from the inside. The Commander wants to talk to him about Tyr's Hand, and about Hearthglen.

They're camped inside the Bulwark now, at the far west of the Plaguelands. It's a long way, so fly. Give it to Rory and tell him the Commander would like an answer, not a sermon.

plw_the_sexton.accept_text:
Edda Marris came to the chapel about her family's crypt, and the chapel means me. The family's sexton buried every Marris for forty years, and he didn't stop when the plague came. Sexton Hollowell is still down there digging, and the dead he's buried sing for him. The Bone Choir, the farmhands called it, before they were in it.

She'd like him put in the ground for good, and the singing stopped. I'll say the words once you've done the rest.

His hall's in the middle of the crypt, and the choir sings from the chapel at the head of it. You'll hear them both. Don't listen to the words, because they'll tell you to lie down.
plw_the_sexton.turn_in_text:
It's gone quiet down there, then. Edda will be glad, though she won't say so.

I'll go down with her next week and we'll say their names together. Somebody in the family should, and she's the only one of them left breathing.

plw_cartmaster_corin.accept_text:
Cartmaster Corin gave the crossing its name. He ran a carting business there before the plague, and now he runs it for the Cult, with the same ledgers and the same smile. I bought every horse in this stable off him, and he gave me a fair price.

Bram says you've cleared the square. I want Corin dead and his ledgers burned.

He's in the old counting house at the crossing. He doesn't fight fair and he'll call everything nearby to help him, so take friends with you.
plw_cartmaster_corin.turn_in_text:
Then the carts stop for good. Bram's burning the counting house tonight, and I've asked to hold the torch.

He gave me a fair price on those horses. I keep thinking about that.

ple_the_bones_of_the_east.accept_text:
I dug coal in the Rhondda, back home, so when Ysolde found out where the east's dead were going, she sent for me. The Scourge has dug a mine under the Pestilent Scar. The Bone Miners in it are digging up the dead to build its constructs, and the Scourge Pit Guards keep them at it.

I want the digging stopped. It's a bad mine, badly propped, and what they're digging up is people.

The mine's in the hill under the Scar. Every gallery's deeper than the last, so it's a long walk down. The pit guards will keep you out if they can.
ple_the_bones_of_the_east.turn_in_text:
Those were people once, the bones they were digging up. Ysolde's going to say the prayer for all of them at once.

I've been reading the Scourge's tallies off the pit walls. Somebody down there weighs everything that comes out, and I'd like him gone next.

ple_the_overseer.accept_text:
The tallies on the pit walls all end at one place. Overseer Marrowgrim sits in the pit at the bottom with a meat hook and a cart, and nothing leaves that mine that he hasn't weighed. We had a man like that at the colliery, and he was a lot less dangerous.

I want him dead before the Scourge has bone enough for another colossus.

He's in the marrow pit at the end of the deepest gallery. He's big and he's slow until he isn't, so don't stand where that hook can reach you, and watch out for the cart.
ple_the_overseer.turn_in_text:
The Scar's quieter already, and Faelis says the bats have stopped circling it.

There's still one more thing down there. Marrowgrim's tallies say everything went somewhere else before it came to him.

ple_the_ossifier.accept_text:
I've found a workshop off the middle of the Bone Mines, and Marrowgrim's tallies say everything the mine digs up goes there first. The Ossifier is a necromancer, and he's the one who turns the east's dead into the Scourge's constructs.

Close his workshop, and I'll bring the roof down on it after.

It's off the middle gallery, up a short passage. He'll be wearing bone armour, and it's thick, so be patient with it. Break that first, then break him.
ple_the_ossifier.turn_in_text:
That's the end of the Bone Mines, and the end of the constructs coming out of them. I'll set the charges tomorrow.

I never liked closing a pit, back home. I'm glad to be closing this one.

pl_ts_invaders_scourgestones.description: Bring Quartermaster Hasana Reed a handful of Invader's Scourgestones from the Scourge in the eastern Plaguelands.
pl_ts_invaders_scourgestones.accept_text:
The Scourge that march in the east carry heavier shards. Invader's Scourgestones, we call them, and they're cold enough to hurt. The dead round Stratholme and Terrordale carry most of them.

Archmage Hale breaks the little ones himself. These go in a lead box under my counter until the Dawn can carry them somewhere safe, and the Dawn pays twice over for every one.

Bring me a handful whenever you can. Wear gloves, because they bite.
pl_ts_invaders_scourgestones.turn_in_text:
These are heavy ones. Every shard here is one less thing walking toward the wall.

Into the box they go. Come back when you've got more.

plw_spores_for_the_sanctuary.accept_text:
Dr. Sun's sealed a sample of the vale's spores in wax, and she's asked me to find somebody going south, because she's busy with the vale. There's a botanist at the Emerald Sanctuary in Felwood, Yuki Hashimoto, who's cataloguing everything that grows back in corrupted ground. If anyone's seen something like this, it's her.

The doctor would like her to compare it with what grows in Felwood.

Take the zeppelin from Tirisfal to Orgrimmar, then go north through Ashenvale to Felwood. Yuki's at the Sanctuary, probably on her knees in a flowerbed. Don't break the wax, and don't let a bat sit on it.

plw_the_three_ziggurats.accept_text:
I fly over Stratholme most days, and from up there you can see what the ground can't. The Scourge raised three ziggurats in the dead half of the city, and each one has a keeper. Nerub'enkan is a spider lord out of the north. Baroness Anastari was a lady of the court and is a banshee now. Maleki the Pallid is a lich who keeps his ziggurat as cold as a tomb.

While those three stand, the Baron's gate stays shut. Osric buries what comes out of the city, and he'd like it to stop. Kill all three keepers and the way opens.

Go in from the service gate, where the Scourge bring their carts.
plw_the_three_ziggurats.turn_in_text:
Then the gate's open. I flew over this morning, and the ziggurats have gone dark.

Osric says he can stop digging for a while. You'll want to go through, I expect.

plw_sigils_of_the_fallen.accept_text:
The Gate Death Knights still wear the sigils of the houses they served when they were alive. Barov, Mardenholde, and a dozen others. Ser Roland says the houses that are left don't know what became of their sons and daughters.

He'd like the sigils back, so he can tell them, and he's asked me to keep the tally while he watches the gate.

The death knights wear them on their breastplates. Cut them off and bring them to me. Ser Roland will know every house by its colours.
plw_sigils_of_the_fallen.turn_in_text:
That's Barov, and that's Mardenholde. Ser Roland says this one's his own cousin's house.

He'll write to every family that's left, and I'll carry the letters. It's the least they deserve.

plw_carrion_grubs.description: Kill Carrion Grubs along the road through the western half of the Eastern Plaguelands.
plw_carrion_grubs.accept_text:
The Carrion Grubs got into the larder at Crown Guard before we left, and now they're all along the road west. They eat everything that dies out there, and then they eat everything that's alive and slow. Kaia's lost every snare she's set this month, and I've lost a cart of turnips.

They swarm the road and the ditches beside it. They're slow and they're soft, but there are always more of them. Burn them if you can, because they don't like it.
plw_carrion_grubs.turn_in_text:
That's the road clear of them for a while, anyway. I'll send the next cart out tomorrow.

Here, take a pie for the road. It isn't crow, I promise.

pln_a_letter_for_brill.accept_text:
Lena's written to the Order's man in Brill, and she's asked me to send it with someone, since I send him a cask of beer every month anyway. Flamewarden Teodor Novak watches the Scarlet Monastery from a window over the inn, and he's very good at it.

If Hale marches out of Hearthglen, the Monastery marches with him. Teodor needs to know what Lena knows.

Go south to the Bulwark and out its west gate into Tirisfal, then on to Brill. Teodor lodges over the inn. He'll offer you a drink, and you should take it. It's my beer, and it's the only good beer in Tirisfal.

pln_travellers_keepsakes.accept_text:
Mateo told me about the Skeletal Wanderers on the roads, and I can't stop thinking about them. This is the last bed before Hearthglen, and some of those travellers might have slept under this roof. If they had pockets, some of them still have whatever was in them. A ring, a letter, a toy for somebody waiting at home.

I'd like to write down what they were. Somebody might still be waiting for one of them, and the Order keeps a book of names at the Bulwark.

They walk the roads all round the Watch. Not every one of them has anything left. Bring me what you find and I'll write it all down.
pln_travellers_keepsakes.turn_in_text:
A pipe, a thimble, a child's wooden horse. Every one of these belonged to somebody.

Odile at the Bulwark will want these for her book. I'll send them south with the next cask.

pln_a_serum_for_felwood.accept_text:
Noah's made a serum. It doesn't cure anything, and he wants me to be clear about that, but it slows the plague down long enough to matter. He asked me to send it with a hawk, and the hawks won't carry glass, so I'm asking you.

There's a doctor at the Emerald Sanctuary in Felwood, Dr. Nkechi Adeyemi, who's treating a sickness that sounds a lot like this one. She sent Noah the kit he's been using all month, and he'd like to send her something back.

Take the zeppelin from Tirisfal to Orgrimmar, then go north through Ashenvale to Felwood. The Sanctuary's the clean glade in the middle of it. Keep the vial out of the sun.

pln_plague_bats.accept_text:
The Plague Bats come out over the Thondroril at dusk, and they've started going for my hawks. Oona's been fighting them off the river with a fishing rod, and I've lost a hawk to them already this month. I'm sure they carry the plague.

They roost in the trees along the river. They're fast, so don't chase them. Stand still on the bank and let them come to you, because they will.
pln_plague_bats.turn_in_text:
The hawks can fly at dusk again, and Oona can fish. That's a better evening for everyone.

Here's something for your trouble, and Oona says she'll keep a fish back for you at supper.

pln_high_inquisitor_faulk.accept_text:
High Inquisitor Faulk runs the inquisition at Hearthglen. He kept me in a cell there for a month. He's the one who decided the newcomers were the Scourge's agents, and Amalie says he decided it on a Tuesday, between breakfast and prayers.

On feast days he walks the fields himself, with the Hearthglen Inquisitors at his back. Today's a feast day.

He'll be in Hearthglen Fields, below the walls, close to the gate. He's got a temper and a lot of fire, and he heals himself when he's hurt. Bring friends, and bring someone who can stop his prayers.
pln_high_inquisitor_faulk.turn_in_text:
Then it's done, and the inquisition's got nobody to lead it.

I keep waiting to feel something. I think maybe I feel lighter. I'll tell Amalie tonight.

pln_saw_blades.accept_text:
My father can't cut timber without saws, and the Crusade took every saw in the Plaguelands up to the Northridge Lumber Camp. He's been shaping planks with a hatchet, and it shows. He won't ask anyone for help, so I'm asking for him.

The Scarlet Lumberjacks carry good steel blades, forged in Hearthglen. They carry them on their backs in the woods.

Bring me the blades and leave the handles. He'll want to make his own handles. He's a carpenter, not a smith, and he'll tell you so.
pln_saw_blades.turn_in_text:
These are beautiful blades. Hearthglen's smiths know their business, I'll give them that.

Don't tell my father I asked. We'll have a proper sawpit at the Watch by the end of the week, and he can think it was his idea.

pls_the_writhing_haunt.turn_in_text:
Something's moving in this one. Look at that.

I need someone who knows more about the walking dead than I do, and the only one I trust is on the other side of the sea. Surgeon Grey's sending a case to her for me, so go and see him a few doors along the street.

plw_the_crossings_abominations.turn_in_text:
That's the crossing's muscle gone.

There's only one man left running the carts. Hob Kettering, our stablemaster, knows him better than I do. He's just along from me, and he'd like a word with you.

plw_the_family_crypt.turn_in_text:
Thank you. My husband's grandmother is down there somewhere, and I hope she's back where she belongs.

There's more, though. Something's still singing down there, and it isn't any hymn I know. I've asked Brother Anselm at the chapel to help, so go and see him.

sps_deserter_tags.description:
Sergeant Dallow and I keep the March between us. He keeps the soldiers, and I keep their kit and their roll. Every soldier in the March carries an iron tag with a number stamped on it, and every number matches a line in my book.

The deserters at Valgan's Field still wear theirs. Somebody from the Undercity will come down this road one day and ask how many walked off, and they'll want to hear that it was a few. Dallow wants to tell them who, and by what number, and he'll read it out of my book.

Take the tags off the Field Deserters and bring them to me.
sps_deserter_tags.accept_text: Iron tags, stamped with a number. Off the deserters at Valgan's Field.
sps_deserter_tags.turn_in_text:
That's every number I needed, and I'll enter each one against the roll tonight, in ink.

Dallow can open the book now and tell the Undercity exactly who walked off. A list of names is a lot harder to wave away than a guess.

sps_pyre_cultists.description:
The cult in Pyrewood has taken the burned houses at the south end of the village, and they cast over the dead hearths, the stone ones that are all that's left of those homes. Brand's listened from the lane, and he doesn't know the name they pray to. He was the hearthwarden here when the village had people in it, so he's heard most of them.

Loremaster Sennarath sent me to copy their marks, and I can't get near enough to copy anything while they're in there. Brand says something answers when they call, and I believe him.

Clear the Pyrewood Cultists out of the burned houses, and I'll go in after you and start copying.
sps_pyre_cultists.accept_text: The burned houses at the south end of Pyrewood. They cast over the dead hearths.
sps_pyre_cultists.turn_in_text:
Nothing answered tonight. Brand stood in the lane for an hour to be sure, and so did I.

The walls in those houses are covered in the cult's marks. I'll be copying them for a week.

sps_pyre_sigils.description:
Every one of the cultists carries an iron sigil. Brand took one off a body and gave it to me, and it's properly cut, not scratched. That means somebody had these made by a smith, and in a quantity, for a cult living in burned houses in a village with nobody alive in it.

The Loremaster reads this sort of cipher. I'd rather send him a handful than the one, because a handful lets him lay them side by side.

Take the sigils off the Pyrewood Cultists and bring them to me.
sps_pyre_sigils.accept_text: Iron sigils, off the Pyrewood Cultists. They're stamped, not scratched.
sps_pyre_sigils.turn_in_text:
They aren't all the same. Look, that one and that one are different at the edge.

So the cipher has variants, and that's a rank, or a house, or a posting. These people are organised somewhere other than here, and the Loremaster's going to want to know where.

sps_ashes_south.description:
Brand scraped a phial of ash off the hall steps the night the doors were barred, and he gave it to me, because neither of us knows what's in it. The cult burned something in that hall, and it wasn't wood. Brand's been a hearthwarden his whole life, and he says it went to ash the wrong colour and it hasn't stopped being warm.

There's nobody in Silverpine who can tell us what it is. There's an apothecary at Southpoint Tower, down in Hillsbrad, who's had nothing but blight to work on for years and who'll probably open it in the road.

Take it to her anyway. I'd rather have a reckless answer than none.
sps_ashes_south.accept_text: To the apothecary at Southpoint Tower in Hillsbrad. She'll probably open it in the road.
sps_ashes_south.turn_in_text:
You've come from Pyrewood? Give it here, I'm not waiting until I'm indoors.

This isn't from here. I don't mean Hillsbrad and I don't mean Silverpine. I've handled blight from every corner of this continent, and this ash isn't from any of it.

Sit down and start at the beginning, and don't leave anything out.

sps_sfk_hounds.description:
I hunt the hills for the Rear Guard's table, and I know what a wolf does when it's hungry. The worgs in Shadowfang Keep don't do any of it. They're Arugal's own, kennelled and fed on a schedule, on things that used to be people.

Rynn says a fed worg isn't a wolf any more, because it's never had to fail at a hunt, and she's right. A wolf I can track. These sit in their kennels and wait to be let out.

Thin the kennels before somebody does let them out. Kill the Keep Worgs and the Slavering Worgs both.
sps_sfk_hounds.accept_text: The kennels in Shadowfang Keep, west of the bailey.
sps_sfk_hounds.turn_in_text:
That's a thinner pack, and a fight I can pick instead of one that picks me.

The man who keeps them is still in there, though, and he keeps them hungry.

sps_sfk_rethilgore.description:
Rethilgore keeps the hounds in Shadowfang, and he keeps them hungry on purpose. A fed hound sleeps, and a hungry one watches the door.

He was a decent man in Pyrewood. Brand knew him, and so did half the village. I've watched him through a glass, and he's still careful. He checks the chains and he counts the hounds. There's enough of him left to do the job properly, and not enough to stop doing it.

I'd like him buried. He's in the big pen in the west wing, and he'll have a chain in his hand.
sps_sfk_rethilgore.accept_text: Shadowfang Keep, in the kennels. He's in the big pen in the west wing.
sps_sfk_rethilgore.turn_in_text:
He fed the hounds first, even at the end. You could see it on them.

I can respect that, I suppose, and I'd rather not have had to.

sps_sfk_moonwalkers.description:
I keep the night watch on the Shadowfang gate, and on a full moon you can hear the keep chanting from here. That's the moonwalkers. Arugal's cult is half sorcerers and half worgen who are still turning, and the chanting is how they get the rest of the way.

The darksouls are what's at the end of it. So the keep isn't a garrison with casters in it. The casters are making the garrison, out of whatever walks in.

Go in wherever you hear chanting, and kill the Shadowfang Moonwalkers and the Shadowfang Darksouls. Kill the casters first, every time.
sps_sfk_moonwalkers.accept_text: Shadowfang Keep, on its hill south-west of the Peril. Go wherever you hear chanting, and kill the casters first.
sps_sfk_moonwalkers.turn_in_text:
The chanting stopped early tonight. That's the first quiet full moon I've had on this gate.

They'll make more, but they'll make them slower now.

sps_sfk_pickets.description:
Marl has the days on the Shadowfang gate and I've got the nights, and the road past the pickets is the worst of both. The ghouls and the stalkers crowd it, and they aren't coming down it. They're pressed up against it, facing the keep, as if something inside were calling them.

There's a party going in soon, and I'd rather they spent what they've got inside instead of on the way up.

Clear the Rotting Ghouls and the Feral Worgen Stalkers off the keep road.
sps_sfk_pickets.accept_text: The keep road past Beren's Peril, south of here. They're pressed against it, facing the keep.
sps_sfk_pickets.turn_in_text:
The road's open to the portcullis.

They'll drift back. Whatever's pulling them hasn't stopped pulling, but a party can get up there now without arriving tired.

sps_at_tomes.description:
The tome wraiths in Ambermill Tower are the pages of a book that learned to fly, and Magister Orsolo has asked me to collect them, since I'm the one who writes everything down. They haunt the galleries, and they're all from the same book. Nobody's noticed that, because nobody's held two of them side by side.

The Magister thinks he knows who wrote it. He won't say who until he's sure, and I've stopped asking.

Take the torn pages off the Tome Wraiths, enough that he can lay them out together. And don't read any of it aloud, not even to yourself.
sps_at_tomes.accept_text: Off the Tome Wraiths in the galleries of Ambermill Tower. Don't read aloud.
sps_at_tomes.turn_in_text:
The Magister knows this hand. I watched his face when I showed him.

It was Hawren, who taught him to read. He'll want to see you.

sps_at_spellblades.description:
I was an apprentice at Ambermill's sawmill, under Haskell. Our saws were enchanted to run themselves, and that was his idea, and he was proud of it for years. The Animated Spellblades in the tower carry the same enchantment. They're bright and quick and they don't care who they cut, because nobody gave them the part that decides when to stop.

Two of my friends went into that tower on Haskell's say-so, to see whether the enchantment was the same as ours, and it is. They didn't come out, and he's had the rest of us sorting nails ever since.

Break the spellblades. They're all through the tower, and they're the ones that glint.
sps_at_spellblades.accept_text: The Animated Spellblades, all through Ambermill Tower, through the waygate south-east of here.
sps_at_spellblades.turn_in_text:
It's quieter in there, then. I'll tell Haskell myself.

He won't let us go back in for a month, but at least there's nothing in there now to keep us out.

dk_stray_cull.description:
The dogs and the rats have always come to the graveyard, and we've always let them, because what's in the ground is past caring. Something in the soil has turned them. The Plagued Strays are sick in a way I haven't got a word for, and they've started going for the newly risen.

You'll meet people out there who woke up this week and can't work out which way the village is. They can't defend themselves. A fortnight ago, neither could you.

Thin the strays, and the Grave Rats with them. The rats carry it into the stores, and then it's everyone's problem.
dk_stray_cull.accept_text: Round Deathknell's graves and the gate. Mind the newly risen, because they can't defend themselves.
dk_stray_cull.turn_in_text:
That's the yard safe for the ones still coming up.

You'll see a few of them wandering. Leave them be. They'll find their way, and I'll bury the ones who don't.

dk_scavenger_scraps.description:
I keep Deathknell's stores, and they're shrinking. Nobody here eats, so it isn't food. It's salt tins, rope, bandages and lamp oil, the things that keep a settlement standing.

The Ragged Scavengers out past the fence have been dragging it off, and they take whatever glints without the faintest idea what any of it does.

I want all of it back. The Dark Lady keeps careful accounts and so do I, and that's worth learning on your first day. We aren't animals picking over a ruin.
dk_scavenger_scraps.accept_text: The Burned Farmstead past the fence, where the scavengers den. Bring back every piece, because I'll know what's missing.
dk_scavenger_scraps.turn_in_text:
That's all of it. I've checked it against my list, item by item.

That list is why there's a Deathknell at all. Remember that when somebody tells you we're just corpses that got lucky.

dk_scout_hollow.description:
Gresk thinks the spiders at his claim are wandering in, and they aren't. There are too many and they come too steadily, and a wandering population thins when you cull it. This one doesn't.

There's a cave beside the claim, Night Web's Hollow, and I think it's pouring them out like a spring. Before anybody goes in there to deal with it, Krell wants eyes on the inner strand, and he asked me for a scout. I'm asking you.

Get to the inner strand of the Hollow, look at what's there, and come back out.
dk_scout_hollow.accept_text: Night Web's Hollow, the cave beside the claim. Get to the inner strand and come back out.
dk_scout_hollow.turn_in_text:
A brood chamber, that deep in? Then it's worse than I thought.

Go and tell Krell. He'll want somebody to finish it, and he'll want it to be you.

dk_verrick_crypt.description:
Verrick's been watching the Scarlet Crypt from his rocks for weeks, and he won't go down the nave. I keep crypts myself, so he asked me, and I'm asking you, because my knees won't take those stairs.

It's the Crusade's real foothold in this valley. There's a chapel, an ossuary, a reliquary, and a High Inquisitor who likes confessions. Something is holding the doors at the far end shut, and it isn't a bar.

Walk the nave to the far doors and look at what's holding them. Don't try to clear it. Just look, and come back.
dk_verrick_crypt.accept_text: Down the nave of the Scarlet Crypt to the far doors. Look at what's holding them, then come back.
dk_verrick_crypt.turn_in_text:
Held from the inside, by something that wanted to be in there? Then this stopped being a camp outside a crypt a long time ago.

I'll tell Verrick. He won't like it, but he'll want to know.

dk_verrick_vaults.description:
Verrick tells me the High Inquisitor's dead and the Scarlet Crypt still isn't ours. There are two vaults left, one on either side.

The ossuary's under Valdric Bonewarden. That's where the Crusade put the dead they never finished burying, and most of them are our dead, from this valley. I've been asking to bury them properly since the day I woke up.

The reliquary's on the other side, under Brother Wystan, and whatever the Scarlets thought worth saving is in there. Kill them both and open the vaults, and the crypt belongs to the valley again.
dk_verrick_vaults.accept_text: Both vaults of the Scarlet Crypt: the ossuary under Valdric, and the reliquary under Wystan.
dk_verrick_vaults.turn_in_text:
Both vaults are open, and the whole crypt with them.

I'll start bringing our dead out of the ossuary tomorrow and put them in ground that belongs to them. Whatever's in the reliquary can go to Krell, and then to the Undercity. Go and find Krell, too. He's run out of things to send you at.

ucq_sennarath_scroll.description:
Loremaster Sennarath sealed this scroll in grave-wax and left it with me to send, because he won't let it leave the city except in a steady pair of hands, and he's decided mine shake. He's been tracking the Cult's cipher across half of Lordaeron, and he can read most of it. The rest is a key, and he thinks Keeper Oswin at Raven Hill has it.

Oswin's been reading the same markings on his own stones for longer than the Loremaster's been working, and he's never written any of it down.

Put it in Oswin's hand, and don't open it. The wax only takes one impression, and the Loremaster will know.
ucq_sennarath_scroll.accept_text: Up the shaft into Tirisfal, south through the Rear Guard into Silverpine, and down the Trunk Road to Raven Hill Cemetery on its west side. Give it to Keeper Oswin.
ucq_sennarath_scroll.turn_in_text:
That's Sennarath's seal. He writes the way I read, slowly and twice.

Give me a moment. There'll be a reply, and it'll be shorter than he'd like.

uc_dalaran_question.description:
This is curiosity rather than orders, so you can say no. The Ruins of Dalaran stand at the edge of Hillsbrad under a shield the Kirin Tor raised and have never lowered. I studied under that shield when I was alive, and I've walked round it a great many times since.

Word has reached the Apothecarium that a party of blood elves got underneath it three years ago, when the world shook and a great many sealed things stopped being sealed. If the word's true, they've been living under the ruins ever since. Nobody has confirmed it.

Go and look, and bring me something better than a rumour.
uc_dalaran_question.accept_text: Into eastern Hillsbrad, within sight of the Dalaran shield. Look, but don't start anything.
uc_dalaran_question.turn_in_text:
Lights under the shield, and movement on a schedule? They've been down there three years, the same three years the rest of us have spent learning what the sky's doing now.

This goes to the Apothecarium tonight. I expect somebody more senior than me will want to meet you.

ucq_hillsbrad_writ.description: The Executor signed a writ for the commander at Tarren Mill, and I drew it up for him. It gives her standing authority to act in the valley without writing north first. It sat on his desk for a month, because signing it meant admitting he can't run Hillsbrad from here.
ucq_hillsbrad_writ.accept_text:
Take it south through Silverpine, down into Hillsbrad, and east to Tarren Mill, the mill town cut in half by a water channel. Commander Thorne holds it.

The Executor would rather keep that authority for himself. He signed it anyway, because the other choice was losing the valley by post.
ucq_hillsbrad_writ.turn_in_text:
He signed it? I've been asking for this for two years, and I'd stopped expecting it. This is permission to stop waiting.

There's Alterac money in these hills, there are wizards in a scrap camp, and there's a man in Durnholde keeping a court. I can go after all three now without writing north first.

sm_the_bloodmages_stone.description:
Alchemist Dunmere has heard that the Crusade keeps a blood mage in the Graveyard's tomb, Bloodmage Thalnos, who's kept himself alive a long time on other people.

He wants the stone Thalnos does it with. The Master Apothecary has her own uses for something that keeps a heart beating, and she's asked him to find out how it works.
sm_the_bloodmages_stone.accept_text: Thalnos holds Honor's Tomb, at the far end of the Graveyard past the open burial ground. His ward drinks spells, so hit him with steel. The stone will be on him. Bring it to me, not to the Master Apothecary, because I want a look at it first.
sm_the_bloodmages_stone.turn_in_text:
It's still warm, and it's still beating.

I'll take it apart tonight and send what I learn up to Lorrane. Don't mention it in the tavern.

fen_banshee_locks.description:
When a banshee fades on the strand, she leaves a lock of hair behind, and she does it every time. Gravemoss used to burn them, and I told him to stop, because I think they're anchors. A thing made of grief and air leaves behind the one part of a person that lasts after death, and I don't think that's an accident.

I think that's what holds them to the strand, and it's why they keep coming back however often the village puts them down.

Bring me the locks off the Isle Banshees. I'll bury them under the village stones, in ground that was ours before any of this, and we'll find out whether an old woman is right about something.
fen_banshee_locks.accept_text: Gather the locks the banshees leave behind when they fade on the strand.
fen_banshee_locks.turn_in_text:
I've buried them one at a time, under the stones, and said a name over each. I made the names up, and I won't pretend otherwise.

But a thing in the ground with a name over it makes a grave, and I'd rather they were anchored here than out on the strand.

fen_noble_signets.description:
The Cursed Nobles in Fenris Proper still wear their house signets. They've lost their faces and the use of their hands, and they haven't lost the rings. Merrin noticed it first, and she told me.

I don't want them for the gold. I want the crests. The Rear Guard says Fenris was a minor holding with a minor lord and a local misfortune. I'd like to put the crests on a table in Silverpine and ask them what all those noble houses were doing at a minor lord's table on the night the curse was cast.

It won't change anything on this island, but it'll change how seriously the mainland takes it.
fen_noble_signets.accept_text: Take the rings off the Cursed Nobles in the forecourt and the manor grounds.
fen_noble_signets.turn_in_text: Every one of these is from a different house. The Rear Guard will have to read my next report now.

fen_altar_moonhowl.description:
The Rear Guard wants proof that the curse is still alive before they'll send anyone else to Fenris, and Orlan's told me the best proof there is. The worgen at Shadowpine Altar howl at a moon the cavern can't see. There's no sky down there, and they still howl on the nights the moon is full and stay quiet when it isn't, and they're never wrong.

The wraiths move with them, on the same nights.

Thin the Moonhowl Worgen and the Altar Wraiths, and bring me the moon-fangs off the worgen. Half go to Orlan for the cairn he's building at the stair-head, and half go to Silverpine with my report.
fen_altar_moonhowl.accept_text: It's north-west of here, through the arch in the ridge and down into Shadowpine Altar. The worgen and the wraiths hold its circles and the long roads between, and the fangs come off the worgen.
fen_altar_moonhowl.turn_in_text: That's a cairn's worth for Orlan and a box for the Rear Guard. The curse should keep its distance for a season, and Silverpine should stop calling it a local misfortune.

fen_altar_tael.description:
Orlan's told me about Curse Keeper Tael, in the Moon Circle at Shadowpine Altar. Tael feeds the moonstone whatever the cult throws at it, and he's been doing it for centuries.

Here's what I can't get past. The stone doesn't need a keeper. Orlan's watched long enough to be sure, and the old stories say the same. It does what it does whether Tael's there or not. He isn't keeping the curse going. He's attending it, the way a servant attends a master who's long gone.

That frightens me more than anything else on this island. Kill him, and don't watch the moonstone while you do.
fen_altar_tael.accept_text: Go north-west to Shadowpine Altar, then east through its caverns to the Moon Circle. Don't watch the moonstone.
fen_altar_tael.turn_in_text:
He won't tend it any more. The stone will dim or it won't, and either way I'll sleep better.

The old stories never said what Tael was waiting for. I hope it wasn't us.

etc_warriors.description:
The Boneward studies what's in the cave, and I keep it from walking out. The Scourge Warriors patrol the rib tunnels, and they don't sleep and they don't tire. They're terrible at hiding, though. You can hear them a corridor away.

I've watched a pair of them walk the same rib for days without stopping.

Break the patrols. I want a stretch of that corridor that stays empty for an hour, so Calder can set a lamp in it.
etc_warriors.accept_text: In the rib tunnels of the cave. You'll hear them before you see them.
etc_warriors.turn_in_text:
That's an hour of empty corridor. Calder's already taking a lamp down to the next rib.

It's the first ground anyone's held under that farm.

etc_ghouls.description:
It's the same tunnels and a faster problem. The Scourge Ghouls came down with the Scourge, and they stayed when it left, because the cult keeps a plague cellar down here and leaves things out for them.

So they're fed, and a fed pack isn't the starving rabble you've met out on the glades. They're fast, they hunt properly, and they turn together.

Thin them out, and don't let them get behind you in the ribs.
etc_ghouls.accept_text: Through the ribs. They travel in packs and they turn together.
etc_ghouls.turn_in_text:
That's the pack cut down. The cellar can only grow it back so fast.

The Boneward will want to talk to you about that cellar.

etc_krag.description:
There's a pit west of the ribs, and Ghoulmaster Krag keeps his pack in it. He's lined it with bone, and he feeds the pack on what the cult leaves behind, which is how you get a pack that size this far from anything living.

He doesn't fight at the front. He sends the pack and watches how it goes, and then he changes what he's doing. I've watched him do it, and I didn't enjoy it.

Break the pack where it lives, and then kill Krag.
etc_krag.accept_text: The bone-lined pit, west of the ribs. He sends the pack first and watches.
etc_krag.turn_in_text:
The pit's cold. Krag's what I'd have worried about most if we'd come back in a year.

Without Krag, the rest of them are only hungry, and hungry I can handle.

sep_marrow.description:
I sell preserving salts, and I make the bone dust that goes in them. The best bone in this valley is on the Risen Husks out at Raven Hill Cemetery, and Yseult will tell you the same, because she buys from me.

Fresh bone's too wet, and old grave-bone crumbles. The husks are dry all the way through, and the marrow keeps.

Bring me dry marrow-bones off the Risen Husks. If it's damp in your hand, it's no use to me, so leave it where it is.
sep_marrow.accept_text: Off the Risen Husks at Raven Hill Cemetery, wherever the field is thickest.
sep_marrow.turn_in_text:
They're dry and pale, every one of them. That's salt enough for the whole Sepulcher this winter.

Yseult will want the long bones for her combs. I'll let her have them, if she asks nicely.

spn_wl_larder.description:
I read the names on the stones, because somebody should. Corvane's told me what he wants to know about the Widow's Lair, and he can't bring himself to go and find out, so I've said I'd ask for him.

He wants to know how many people that hive has eaten, and he doesn't want a rough number. He's spent years telling families in these woods that their people were lost to wolves, or to the road, and he believed most of it when he said it.

The answer's in two places, deep in the lair. The Larder is where they hang the fresh ones, and the Husk Pit, at the other end, is where they drop what's left. Stand in each long enough to count, and don't bring anything out.
spn_wl_larder.accept_text: The Larder and the Husk Pit, deep in the Widow's Lair. Count, and bring nothing out.
spn_wl_larder.turn_in_text:
Then it's more than either of us wanted. I'll cut every one of them into a stone, even without names, and Corvane can write to the families.

They'll hate him for it, and he says they'll be right to.

sm_the_flamekeepers_due.description:
Renee keeps the inn where Novak lodges, and Novak's left Stane's signet with her for you, with a letter. He wants it put into Flamekeeper Rory Callahan's hand at the Bulwark, the Forsaken's wall at the end of Tirisfal's east road, where the Order keeps its quarter.

The road there runs into country that kills people who aren't ready for it. Novak says to wait until you are, and then to go.
sm_the_flamekeepers_due.accept_text: Take the east road out of Tirisfal to the Bulwark. The Order's banners are on the south side of the street, and Rory stands at the keep's door. Novak says don't go before you're ready, and he means it.

sps_pyre_hall.turn_in_text:
You heard a voice giving orders? There's nobody in that hall to give orders to, and there hasn't been since before the worgen. Either he's talking to the dead, or the dead are in there with him and listening.

I scraped a phial of ash off those steps the night the doors were barred, and I gave it to Avery Lusk by the fire. He'll want you to carry it south.

dk_verrick_fairbanks.turn_in_text:
That's Fairbanks closed. I've carried his tally in my head for a week, and I'd started adding to it in my sleep.

The crypt's vaults are still shut, though. Sexton Marrow wants our dead out of the ossuary, and he'll tell you about it. He's down at the graves.

fen_isle_banshees.turn_in_text:
Nothing answered last night. The drowned still sang, and I sat and listened to the whole of it, and it was just a sound in the dark, the way it was when I was a boy.

Old Wenna's been asking after the banshees. She has a theory about them, and she'd like a word with you.

sm_the_captain_of_the_doors.turn_in_text:
That's the ring. I've seen it on his hand in a doorway with the fire behind him.

Rory should hear it from the one who did it. I'm writing to him tonight, and I'll leave the letter and the ring with Renee downstairs. Collect them from her when you're ready for the road east.
